T0608.title: Teleoperation
T0608.definition: A control mode where an operator remotely controls a robot to perform actions via a communication channel; a common operation mode for humanoid, surgical, and hazardous-operation robots.
T0608.description: Teleoperation lets an operator send control commands from a remote master device while the robot executes on-site, suitable for scenarios humans cannot directly reach (remote surgery, hazardous-material handling, space exploration). But teleoperation relies on a communication channel with risks of hijacking, replay, and latency injection. The Raven II surgical-robot teleoperation hijacking research first revealed its security flaws, able to trigger emergency stops or perform man-in-the-middle attacks. Teleoperation is latency-sensitive; 0–500 ms delays significantly affect performance and operator cognitive response. Quadruped-robot teleoperation has unique attack surfaces like dynamic stability and gait-dependent vulnerability windows.
T0608.usageExample: When a surgeon teleoperates a remote surgical robot, a hijacked channel could let an attacker tamper with surgical-instrument actions, endangering the patient's life.
